blocks.tex: \textbf{5}\quad\text{The graph of }y=x^3+bx^2+cx+d\text{ is shown opposite, where }b,c,d\text{ are real constants.}\quad\begin{array}{ll}\textbf{a}&\text{Find the values of }b,c,d.\quad\text{(3 marks)}\\\textbf{b}&\text{Write down the coordinates of the point where the curve crosses the }y\text{-axis. (1 mark)}\end{array}
\begin{aligned}\textbf{a}\quad y&=x^3+bx^2+cx+d\\y&=(x+3)(x+2)(x-1)\\&=(x+3)(x^2+x-2)\\&=x^3+4x^2+x-6\\&b=4,\ c=1,\ d=-6\end{aligned}
\textbf{b}\quad\text{When }x=0,\ y=-6.\text{ So the curve crosses the }y\text{-axis at }(0,-6).
\textbf{6}\quad\text{The graph of }y=ax^3+bx^2+cx+d\text{ is shown opposite, where }a,b,c,d\text{ are real constants. Find the values of }a,b,c,d.\quad\text{(4 marks)}

\begin{aligned}y&=ax^3+bx^2+cx+d\\y&=a(x+1)(x-2)(x-3)\\&=a(x+1)(x^2-5x+6)\\&=a(x^3-4x^2+x+6)\\&\text{The curve crosses the }y\text{-axis at }(0,2),\text{ so when }x=0,\ y=2.\\2&=a(0-0+0+6)\\a&=\tfrac13\\y&=\tfrac13(x^3-4x^2+x+6)\\&=\tfrac13x^3-\tfrac43x^2+\tfrac13x+2\\&a=\tfrac13,\ b=-\tfrac43,\ c=\tfrac13,\ d=2\end{aligned}

\textbf{7}\quad\text{Given that }\mathrm f(x)=(x-10)(x^2-2x)+12x\quad\begin{array}{ll}\textbf{a}&\text{Express }\mathrm f(x)\text{ in the form }x(ax^2+bx+c)\text{ where }a,b,c\text{ are real constants.}\\\textbf{b}&\text{Hence factorise }\mathrm f(x)\text{ completely.}\\\textbf{c}&\text{Sketch the graph of }y=\mathrm f(x)\text{ showing clearly the points where the graph intersects the axes.}\end{array}
\begin{aligned}\textbf{a}\quad\mathrm f(x)&=(x-10)(x^2-2x)+12x\\&=x^3-12x^2+20x+12x\\&=x^3-12x^2+32x\\&=x(x^2-12x+32)\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}\textbf{b}\quad\mathrm f(x)&=x(x^2-12x+32)\\&=x(x-4)(x-8)\end{aligned}

\textbf{4}\quad\text{Sketch the graph of }y=(x+5)(x-4)(x^2+5x+14).

\begin{aligned}\textbf{a}\quad y&=x^4+bx^3+cx^2+dx+e\\y&=(x+2)(x+1)(x-2)(x-3)\\&\text{When }x=0,\ y=2\times1\times-2\times-3=12\\&\text{So the curve crosses the }y\text{-axis at point }P,\text{ which has coordinates }(0,12).\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}y&=(x+5)(x-4)(x^2+5x+14)\\&\text{The discriminant of the quadratic factor}\\&=b^2-4ac\\&=5^2-4\times1\times14\\&=-31,\text{ so there are no real roots.}\\0&=(x+5)(x-4)(x^2+5x+14)\\&x=-5,\ x=4\text{ or }x^2+5x+14=0\\&\text{The curve crosses the }x\text{-axis at }(-5,0)\text{ and }(4,0).\\&\text{When }x=0,\ y=5\times(-4)\times14=-280\\&\text{So the curve crosses the }y\text{-axis at }(0,-280).\\&x\to\infty,\ y\to\infty\\&x\to-\infty,\ y\to\infty\end{aligned}

blocks.tex: \textbf{5 a}\quad\text{On the same axes sketch the curves given by }y=x^2(x+a)\text{ and }y=\frac bx\text{ where }a,b\text{ are both positive constants. (5 marks)}\quad\textbf{b}\quad\text{Using your sketch, state, giving a reason, the number of real solutions to the equation }x^4+ax^3-b=0.\text{ (1 mark)}

\begin{aligned}\textbf{a}\quad y&=x^2(x-a)\\0&=x^2(x-a)\\&\text{So }x=0\text{ or }x=a\\&\text{The curve crosses the }x\text{-axis at }(a,0)\text{ and touches it at }(0,0).\\&x\to\infty,\ y\to\infty\\&x\to-\infty,\ y\to-\infty\\&y=\frac bx\text{ is a }y=\frac kx\text{ graph, with }k>0.\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}\textbf{b}\quad&\text{From the sketch, there are two points of intersection of the curves. This means there are two values of }x\text{ where}\\&x^2(x-a)=\frac bx\\&x^3(x-a)=b\\&x^4-ax^3-b=0\\&\text{So this equation has two real solutions.}\end{aligned}

\textbf{6 a}\quad\text{On the same set of axes sketch the graphs of }y=\frac4{x^2}\text{ and }y=3x+7.\text{ (3 marks)}\quad\begin{array}{ll}\textbf{b}&\text{Write down the number of real solutions to the equation }\frac4{x^2}=3x+7.\text{ (1 mark)}\\\textbf{c}&\text{Show that you can rearrange the equation to give }(x+1)(x+2)(3x-2)=0.\text{ (2 marks)}\\\textbf{d}&\text{Hence determine the exact coordinates of the points of intersection. (3 marks)}\end{array}
\textbf{b}\quad\text{There are three points of intersection, so there are three real solutions to the equation }\frac4{x^2}=3x+7.

\begin{aligned}\textbf{d}\quad&(x+1)(x+2)(3x-2)=0\\&\text{So }x=-1,\ x=-2\text{ or }x=\tfrac23\\&\text{Using }y=3x+7:\\&\text{when }x=-1,\ y=3(-1)+7=4\\&\text{when }x=-2,\ y=3(-2)+7=1\\&\text{when }x=\tfrac23,\ y=3(\tfrac23)+7=9\\&\text{So the points of intersection are }(-1,4),(-2,1)\text{ and }(\tfrac23,9).\end{aligned}

\textbf{10 a}\quad\text{Sketch the graphs of }y=x^2+1\text{ and }2y=x-1.\quad\begin{array}{ll}\textbf{b}&\text{Explain why there are no real solutions to the equation }2x^2-x+3=0.\\\textbf{c}&\text{Work out the range of values of }a\text{ such that the graphs of }y=x^2+a\text{ and }2y=x-1\\&\text{have two points of intersection.}\end{array}

\begin{aligned}\textbf{b}\quad&\text{From the sketch, there are no points of intersection of the curves. This means there are no values of }x\text{ where}\\&x^2+1=\tfrac12x-\tfrac12\\&2x^2+2=x-1\\&2x^2-x+3=0\\&\text{So this equation has no real solutions.}\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}\textbf{c}\quad x^2+a&=\tfrac12x-\tfrac12\\2x^2+2a&=x-1\\2x^2-x+2a+1&=0\\&\text{Using the discriminant for two real roots,}\\b^2-4ac&>0\\(-1)^2-4(2)(2a+1)&>0\\1-16a-8&>0\\-16a-7&>0\\16a&<-7\\a&<-\tfrac7{16}\end{aligned}

blocks.tex: \textbf{7}\quad\text{The point }P(4,-1)\text{ lies on the curve with equation }y=\mathrm f(x).\quad\begin{array}{ll}\textbf{a}&\text{State the coordinates that point }P\text{ is transformed to on the curve with equation }y=\mathrm f(x-2).\\\textbf{b}&\text{State the coordinates that point }P\text{ is transformed to on the curve with equation }y=\mathrm f(x)+3.\end{array}

\textbf{8}\quad\text{The graph of }y=\mathrm f(x)\text{ where }\mathrm f(x)=\frac1x\text{ is translated so that the asymptotes are at }x=4\text{ and }y=0.\text{ Write down the equation for the transformed function in the form }y=\frac1{x+a}.
\textbf{a}\quad y=\mathrm f(x-2)\text{ is a translation of the graph of }\mathrm f(x)\text{ by }\binom20,\text{ or two units to the right. So }P\text{ translates to }(6,-1).
\textbf{b}\quad y=\mathrm f(x)+3\text{ is a translation of the graph of }\mathrm f(x)\text{ by }\binom03,\text{ or three units up. So }P\text{ translates to }(4,2).

\begin{aligned}&y=\mathrm f(x)\text{ has asymptotes at }x=0\text{ and }y=0.\\&\text{Asymptotes after the translation are at }x=4\text{ and }y=0,\text{ therefore the graph has been translated four units to the right.}\\&\mathrm f(x)=\frac1x,\quad\mathrm f(x-4)=\frac1{x-4}\\&y=\frac1{x-4}\end{aligned}

\textbf{11 a}\quad\text{Sketch the graph of }y=x^3+4x^2+4x.\quad\textbf{b}\quad\text{The point with coordinates }(-1,0)\text{ lies on the curve with equation }y=(x+a)^3+4(x+a)^2+4(x+a)\text{ where }a\text{ is a constant. Find the two possible values of }a.

\textbf{b}\quad y=(x+a)^3+4(x+a)^2+4(x+a).\quad y=x^3+4x^2+4x\text{ crosses the }x\text{-axis at }(0,0)\text{ and }(-2,0).\text{ So for the point }(-1,0)\text{ to lie on the curve, the graph must be translated either one unit to the left or one unit to the right.}\quad a=-1\text{ or }a=1

\textbf{12 a}\quad\text{Sketch the graph of }y=x(x+1)(x+3)^2.\quad\textbf{b}\quad\text{Find the possible values of }b\text{ such that the point }(2,0)\text{ lies on the curve with equation }y=(x+b)(x+b+1)(x+b+3)^2.

\textbf{b}\quad y=(x+b)(x+b+1)(x+b+3)^2.\quad y=x(x+1)(x+3)^2\text{ crosses the }x\text{-axis at }(0,0),(-1,0)\text{ and }(-3,0).\text{ So for the point }(2,0)\text{ to lie on the curve, the graph must be translated either two units to the right, three units to the right or five units to the right.}\quad b=-2,\ b=-3\text{ or }b=-5

\textbf{7}\quad\text{The point }P(2,-3)\text{ lies on the curve with equation }y=\mathrm f(x).\quad\begin{array}{ll}\textbf{a}&\text{State the coordinates that point }P\text{ is transformed to on the curve with equation }y=\mathrm f(2x).\\\textbf{b}&\text{State the coordinates that point }P\text{ is transformed to on the curve with equation }y=4\mathrm f(x).\end{array}

\textbf{8}\quad\text{The point }Q(-2,8)\text{ lies on the curve with equation }y=\mathrm f(x).\text{ State the coordinates that point }Q\text{ is transformed to on the curve with equation }y=\mathrm f(\tfrac12x).

\textbf{a}\quad y=\mathrm f(2x)\text{ is a stretch with scale factor }\frac12\text{ in the }x\text{-direction, so all }x\text{-coordinates are halved.}\quad P(2,-3)\text{ is transformed to the point }(1,-3).

\textbf{b}\quad y=4\mathrm f(x)\text{ is a stretch with scale factor 4 in the }y\text{-direction, so all }y\text{-coordinates are multiplied by four.}\quad P(2,-3)\text{ is transformed to the point }(2,-12).
\mathrm f(\tfrac12x)\text{ is a stretch with scale factor 2 in the }x\text{-direction, so all }x\text{-coordinates are doubled.}\quad Q(-2,8)\text{ is transformed to the point }(-4,8).
\textbf{9 a}\quad\text{Sketch the graph of }y=(x-2)(x-3)^2.\quad\textbf{b}\quad\text{The graph of }y=(ax-2)(ax-3)^2\text{ passes through the point }(1,0).\text{ Find two possible values for }a.

\textbf{b}\quad\mathrm f(x)=(x-2)(x-3)^2.\quad y=(ax-2)(ax-3)^2\text{ is the graph of }y=\mathrm f(ax),\text{ which is a stretch with scale factor }\frac1a\text{ in the }x\text{-direction, so all }x\text{-coordinates are multiplied by }\frac1a.\text{ For the coordinate }(2,0)\text{ to be transformed to }(1,0),\text{ multiply the }x\text{-coordinate by }\frac12,\text{ giving }a=2.\text{ For the coordinate }(3,0)\text{ to be transformed to }(1,0),\text{ multiply the }x\text{-coordinate by }\frac13,\text{ giving }a=3,\ a=2\text{ or }a=3.

\textbf{5}\quad\text{The point }P(2,1)\text{ lies on the graph with equation }y=\mathrm f(x).\quad\begin{array}{ll}\textbf{a}&\text{On the graph of }y=\mathrm f(ax),\text{ the point }P\text{ is mapped to the point }Q(4,1).\text{ Determine the value of }a.\\\textbf{b}&\text{Write down the coordinates of the point to which }P\text{ maps under each transformation}\\\textbf{i}&\mathrm f(x-4)\qquad\textbf{ii}\ 3\mathrm f(x)\qquad\textbf{iii}\ \tfrac12\mathrm f(x)-4\end{array}

\begin{aligned}\textbf{a}\quad&P(2,1)\text{ is mapped to }Q(4,1).\\&\text{The }x\text{-coordinate has doubled, which is a stretch with scale factor 2 in the }x\text{-direction.}\\&y=\mathrm f(\tfrac12x)\\&a=\tfrac12\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}\textbf{b i}\quad&\mathrm f(x-4)\text{ is a translation by }\binom40,\text{ or four units to the right.}\\&\text{So }P\text{ is mapped to }(6,1).\\\textbf{ii}\quad&3\mathrm f(x)\text{ is a stretch with scale factor 3 in the }y\text{-direction.}\\&\text{So }P\text{ is mapped to }(2,3).\\\textbf{iii}\quad&\tfrac12\mathrm f(x)-4\text{ is a stretch with scale factor }\tfrac12\text{ in the }y\text{-direction and then a translation}\\&\text{by }\binom0{-4},\text{ or four units down.}\\&\text{So }P\text{ is mapped to }(2,-3\tfrac12).\end{aligned}

\textbf{6}\quad\text{The diagram shows a sketch of a curve with equation }y=\mathrm f(x).\text{ The points }A(-1,0),B(0,2),C(1,2),D(2,0)\text{ lie on the curve. Sketch the following graphs and give the coordinates of the points }A,B,C,D\text{ after each transformation:}
\textbf{a}\quad y+2=\mathrm f(x)\qquad\textbf{b}\quad\tfrac12y=\mathrm f(x)
\textbf{c}\quad y-3=\mathrm f(x)\qquad\textbf{d}\quad3y=\mathrm f(x)
\textbf{e}\quad2y-1=\mathrm f(x)
